geography_registry.scope: Relationships from the downloaded Montgomery County ACS block-group reporting identifiers only.
geography_registry.basis: GEO_ID decomposition within ACS 2023 reporting geography. No polygons or equivalence between boundary vintages are provided. Parent nodes have no direct estimates and no worker totals or margins are inferred. Available-child counts describe the downloaded subset, never complete county/tract coverage. Airport/World Bank region identifiers remain separate; no automatic cross-source geography join is implied.

job_od.scope: Maryland workplaces only; residence counties elsewhere appear only when linked to an included Maryland workplace. Missing pairs are not asserted to be zero.
job_od.limitations: 2020 JT00 all-job workplace/residence relationships for Maryland workplace counties only. Jobs are not unique people, commuters, trips, daily movements or freight. No transportation mode or route is reported. Upstream disclosure protection and estimation apply. Original publisher release, exact LODES format and boundary vintages were not retained by the mirror and are unverified. Internal totals reconcile, but source accuracy and completeness have not been independently audited. No equivalence to ACS or another archive geography version, or independent survey periods, is inferred.

population_backtest.limitations: Ex-post backtest on the currently downloaded historical population series, not archived as-of publisher releases. Revisions can change results. Training and held-out windows overlap, so errors are not independent trials. No confidence interval, calibrated forecast, transportation-demand forecast or future accuracy guarantee is implied.
population_backtest.basis: Five consecutive training years ending at each origin; targets one or three years later. Only pre-origin history is fitted. Future reference years after the current UTC year are excluded from training and held-out scoring. Last-observed-value forecast is the reference. No missing years are imputed.

road_activity.period_comparison_basis: Same month and January-through-selected-month totals versus the previous calendar year. Each YTD total requires every source month in its own window. Missing inputs and zero references have no percentage. Source hashes/URLs for YTD describe available contributing rows, even when incomplete and the total is null. No annualization, seasonality correction, uncertainty or causal inference.
road_activity.basis: Annual totals sum exactly 12 source-estimated calendar months. Miles per resident use the same-year US population; absent denominators remain null. Partial years are never annualized.
road_activity.limitations: Historical FHWA/FRED numeric archive through August 2023, not seasonally adjusted. Mirror retrieval is not source-release vintage. Estimates may have been revised since this archive. Combined passenger/freight road travel; no link, vehicle, commodity or OD detail. Miles per resident are aggregate road use, not an individual's travel.

commuting.limitations: Workers 16 years and over by residence and usual commuting means, including working from home. Five-year values are survey period estimates, not sums of five annual counts. Estimates are not observed trips, unique daily travelers, OD flows or current conditions. Margins of error are published 90% ACS margins in workers; share percentages are descriptive ratios with no derived margin. Category margins must not be added. Denominator, aggregate, exclusive-mode and detail rows overlap; never sum all records. Carpool-size estimates count workers, not vehicles or measured vehicle occupancy. Geography is the ACS 2023 reporting geography; no temporal boundary crosswalk is implied. No county total is inferred from this downloaded subset.

county_income.attribution: US Census Bureau ACS B19013, 2019–2023 five-year household estimates; pinned numerical archive
county_income.limitations: Downloaded county/county-equivalent archive for 50 states and DC; publisher completeness and release date unverified. Household medians are not additive totals, worker incomes, annual 2023 incomes or current conditions. Amounts are in 2023 inflation-adjusted dollars. Published income margins are in dollars at 90% confidence; no derived uncertainty or significance is calculated. Missing estimates are unavailable, never zero-filled. Reporting identifiers do not establish boundary equivalence with 2020 reference names, job archives or other sources. No commuting behavior, causal relationship or IPF hard control is inferred.

county_age.source_notes_text:
============================================================================================================= Notes ============================================================================================================= Although the American Community Survey (ACS) produces population, demographic and housing unit estimates, the decennial census is the official source of population totals for April 1st of each decennial year. In between censuses, the Census Bureau's Population Estimates Program produces and disseminates the official estimates of the population for the nation, states, counties, cities, and towns and estimates of housing units and the group quarters population for states and counties.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Information about the American Community Survey (ACS) can be found on the ACS website<\/a>. Supporting documentation including code lists, subject definitions, data accuracy, and statistical testing, and a full list of ACS tables and table shells (without estimates) can be found on the Technical Documentation<\/a> section of the ACS website.

Sample size and data quality measures (including coverage rates, allocation rates, and response rates) can be found on the American Community Survey website in the Methodology<\/a> section.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2019-2023 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ACS data generally reflect the geographic boundaries of legal and statistical areas as of January 1 of the estimate year. For more information, see Geography Boundaries by Year<\/a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Data are based on a sample and are subject to sampling variability. The degree of uncertainty for an estimate arising from sampling variability is represented through the use of a margin of error. The value shown here is the 90 percent margin of error. The margin of error can be interpreted roughly as providing a 90 percent probability that the interval defined by the estimate minus the margin of error and the estimate plus the margin of error (the lower and upper confidence bounds) contains the true value. In addition to sampling variability, the ACS estimates are subject to nonsampling error (for a discussion of nonsampling variability, see ACS Technical Documentation<\/a>). The effect of nonsampling error is not represented in these tables.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Users must consider potential differences in geographic boundaries, questionnaire content or coding, or other methodological issues when comparing ACS data from different years. Statistically significant differences shown in ACS Comparison Profiles, or in data users' own analysis, may be the result of these differences and thus might not necessarily reflect changes to the social, economic, housing, or demographic characteristics being compared. For more information, see Comparing ACS Data<\/a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The age dependency ratio is derived by dividing the combined under-18 and 65-and-over populations by the 18-to-64 population and multiplying by 100.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The old-age dependency ratio is derived by dividing the population 65 and over by the 18-to-64 population and multiplying by 100.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The child dependency ratio is derived by dividing the population under 18 by the 18-to-64 population and multiplying by 100.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- When information is missing or inconsistent, the Census Bureau logically assigns an acceptable value using the response to a related question or questions. If a logical assignment is not possible, data are filled using a statistical process called allocation, which uses a similar individual or household to provide a donor value. The \"Allocated\" section is the number of respondents who received an allocated value for a particular subject.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Estimates of urban and rural populations, housing units, and characteristics reflect boundaries of urban areas defined based on 2020 Census data. As a result, data for urban and rural areas from the ACS do not necessarily reflect the results of ongoing urbanization.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Explanation of Symbols:
-<\/TD> The estimate could not be computed because there were an insufficient number of sample observations. For a ratio of medians estimate, one or both of the median estimates falls in the lowest interval or highest interval of an open-ended distribution. For a 5-year median estimate, the margin of error associated with a median was larger than the median itself.<\/TD><\/TR>
N<\/TD> The estimate or margin of error cannot be displayed because there were an insufficient number of sample cases in the selected geographic area.<\/TD><\/TR>
(X)<\/TD> The estimate or margin of error is not applicable or not available.<\/TD><\/TR>
median-<\/TD> The median falls in the lowest interval of an open-ended distribution (for example \"2,500-\")<\/TD><\/TR>
median+<\/TD> The median falls in the highest interval of an open-ended distribution (for example \"250,000+\").<\/TD><\/TR>
**<\/TD> The margin of error could not be computed because there were an insufficient number of sample observations.<\/TD><\/TR>
***<\/TD> The margin of error could not be computed because the median falls in the lowest interval or highest interval of an open-ended distribution.<\/TD><\/TR>
*****<\/TD> A margin of error is not appropriate because the corresponding estimate is controlled to an independent population or housing estimate. Effectively, the corresponding estimate has no sampling error and the margin of error may be treated as zero.<\/TD><\/TR><\/TABLE>

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
county_age.attribution: US Census Bureau ACS S0101, 2019–2023 five-year resident population estimates; pinned numerical archive
county_age.limitations: Downloaded county/county-equivalent archive for 50 states and DC; Puerto Rico excluded. Publisher completeness and release date unverified. Five-year survey estimates are not annual 2023 counts, current population or forecasts. Age groups describe residents, not workers, households, trips or travel needs. Total population overlaps the two age cohorts; the cohorts are disjoint but do not cover every age. No remaining cohort, parent geography total or travel rate is inferred. Numeric margins are published 90% sampling margins. The original ***** marker denotes control to an independent population/housing estimate; no numeric margin or confidence interval is substituted. Census permits zero sampling MOE for these controlled estimates, but nonsampling error is not represented. Shares are descriptive with no derived margin or significance. source_quality.source_notes_text:
============================================================================================================= Notes ============================================================================================================= Although the American Community Survey (ACS) produces population, demographic and housing unit estimates, the decennial census is the official source of population totals for April 1st of each decennial year. In between censuses, the Census Bureau's Population Estimates Program produces and disseminates the official estimates of the population for the nation, states, counties, cities, and towns and estimates of housing units and the group quarters population for states and counties.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Information about the American Community Survey (ACS) can be found on the ACS website<\/a>. Supporting documentation including code lists, subject definitions, data accuracy, and statistical testing, and a full list of ACS tables and table shells (without estimates) can be found on the Technical Documentation<\/a> section of the ACS website.

Sample size and data quality measures (including coverage rates, allocation rates, and response rates) can be found on the American Community Survey website in the Methodology<\/a> section.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2019-2023 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ACS data generally reflect the geographic boundaries of legal and statistical areas as of January 1 of the estimate year. For more information, see Geography Boundaries by Year<\/a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Data are based on a sample and are subject to sampling variability. The degree of uncertainty for an estimate arising from sampling variability is represented through the use of a margin of error. The value shown here is the 90 percent margin of error. The margin of error can be interpreted roughly as providing a 90 percent probability that the interval defined by the estimate minus the margin of error and the estimate plus the margin of error (the lower and upper confidence bounds) contains the true value. In addition to sampling variability, the ACS estimates are subject to nonsampling error (for a discussion of nonsampling variability, see ACS Technical Documentation<\/a>). The effect of nonsampling error is not represented in these tables.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Users must consider potential differences in geographic boundaries, questionnaire content or coding, or other methodological issues when comparing ACS data from different years. Statistically significant differences shown in ACS Comparison Profiles, or in data users' own analysis, may be the result of these differences and thus might not necessarily reflect changes to the social, economic, housing, or demographic characteristics being compared. For more information, see Comparing ACS Data<\/a>.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The age dependency ratio is derived by dividing the combined under-18 and 65-and-over populations by the 18-to-64 population and multiplying by 100.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The old-age dependency ratio is derived by dividing the population 65 and over by the 18-to-64 population and multiplying by 100.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The child dependency ratio is derived by dividing the population under 18 by the 18-to-64 population and multiplying by 100.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- When information is missing or inconsistent, the Census Bureau logically assigns an acceptable value using the response to a related question or questions. If a logical assignment is not possible, data are filled using a statistical process called allocation, which uses a similar individual or household to provide a donor value. The \"Allocated\" section is the number of respondents who received an allocated value for a particular subject.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Estimates of urban and rural populations, housing units, and characteristics reflect boundaries of urban areas defined based on 2020 Census data. As a result, data for urban and rural areas from the ACS do not necessarily reflect the results of ongoing urbanization.

coverage.name: County resident age profile
coverage.detail: ACS2019–2023 county total, under 18 and 65-plus resident estimates; controlled/numeric/unavailable margins distinct. No current counts, travel needs, trips or remaining cohorts inferred.

coverage.name: County household income
coverage.detail: Separate ACS2019–2023 county/county-equivalent household medians in2023inflation-adjusted dollars; published90%MOEs and unavailable cells retained. No sums of medians, worker-income or boundary equivalence inferred.

coverage.name: Historical Virginia workplace job OD
coverage.detail: Separate2020 Virginia workplace county archive; jobs, not people/trips/freight. No pooling with MD/DC or boundary equivalence; exact release/format/boundary vintages unverified.

coverage.name: Historical DC workplace job OD
coverage.detail: Separate 2020 District of Columbia workplace archive; jobs, not unique people, trips or freight. No pooling with Maryland, no mode split, exact release/boundary vintages unverified.

coverage.name: Historical job residence–workplace OD
coverage.detail: 2020 county-pair archive for Maryland workplaces only. JT00 jobs, not unique people, trips or mode-specific traffic; release and boundary vintages unverified.

coverage.name: Archived rail station points
coverage.detail: Washington metropolitan platform centroids; inventory date and service status unknown. Location assets, not dated observations, entrances, routes or current network coverage.

coverage.name: Block-group commuting survey
coverage.detail: 664 downloaded Montgomery County MD block groups, 2019–2023 ACS worker estimates and margins of error. Not county-wide verified coverage, annual traffic or OD flows.

coverage.name: National annual economy
coverage.detail: US population and nominal GDP; source-dependent annual history.

coverage.name: State airport inventory
coverage.detail: Current inventory counts, including heliports and small airfields; no traffic volumes.

coverage.name: Historical national road activity
coverage.detail: Monthly source-estimated vehicle miles, Jan 1970–Aug 2023 archive; complete-year totals and same-year population ratios. No current operations or link-level counts.

coverage.name: Experimental baseline forecasts
